text: So what changed?

text: Your brain grew. Just one percent.

text: And tomorrow... it's going to grow again.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Here's how it works.

text: Your brain has about eighty-six billion neurons. More brain means more connections, and more connections means more power.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Every day, you get a little more of it.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: But there's one thing that isn't growing.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: The box it lives in.

text: Day three. You read a whole book in the time it takes to make toast.

text: Day twenty. You notice the traffic lights in your town are badly timed.

text: So you email the city a fix.

text: One week later, traffic jams drop by half.

text: And officials say the plan came from... a sixteen-year-old?

text: Then comes the biggest quiz show in the country.

text: Overnight, you're everywhere.

text: Scientists want to study you. Companies want to hire you.

text: People are calling you the Human Supercomputer.

text: Kinda corny.

text: You're literally a supercomputer.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: But by day thirty-five, the headaches start.

text: Your brain burns about twenty percent of your body's energy. A bigger brain wants more.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Five breakfasts. Still hungry.

text: That was the whole fridge.

speaker: YOU
text: I'm thinking a lot.

text: Your favorite cap doesn't fit anymore.

text: And at night, you can hear your own heartbeat in your ears.

text: But the doctor has good news too.

text: We have a treatment. It stops the growth and shrinks your brain back to normal.

text: Back to normal.

text: Back to failing math.

text: We start tomorrow morning.

text: That night, walking down the hallway, you meet a little girl named Lily.

text: Are you the smart guy from TV?

text: ...Yeah. That's me.

text: Lily has a disease so rare that only three hundred people in the world have it.

text: There's no cure.

text: Nobody's found one.

text: But your brain doesn't just read her chart.

text: It sees a pattern nobody else has.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: You're close. You can feel it.

text: But you need one more day of growth to finish it.

text: Take the treatment in the morning, and you're safe.

text: Your life...

text: Your head feels like it's going to split open.

text: You wake up three days later.

text: You're stable. The treatment worked.

text: Your brain is back to normal.
